sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal, Raimund Kastenholz, Ulrich Kleinewillinghöfer & Florian Lionnet. 2018. The Bua Group languages (Chad, Adamawa 13): A comparative perspective. In R. Kramer & R. Kießling (eds.), Current approaches to Adamawa and Gur languages (AuÜ Beiheft 34), 53-126. Köln: Köppe.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent anywhere (grep stress|accent|prominen = 0). Bon Gula data come from Roberts' unpublished 2004 wordlist (p. 59); §4.4 Tones pp. 71-72 characterises Ɓa, Lua, Tun, Bolgo (3 heights) and Kulaal (2 tones) but not Bon Gula; §5.5 p. 97: Bon Gula (Roberts 2004) added to tone Tables 21-22 'but... it is still difficult to derive clear information from sources that are relatively limited and not systematically marked for tones, so that we will in fact not comment on them here'. Table 21 p. 98: Bon Gula noun tone reflexes H, H/HL, LH? with many '?'. References p. 125 list Roberts…

sources.note: Bua languages listed under Middle-Chari stem-initial prominence are Lua and Ɓa only; Bon Gula not covered.

sources.note: 'goula de Bon' appears only in the group inventory; the phonology remarks (3-register tone) cover Tun, Lua and Ɓa. No accent statement for Bon Gula.
